unit.why: A single anecdote: a tzaddik arrives late to Kol Nidre on Yom Kippur eve because he stayed to calm and play with a crying child left alone at home.

stories.start_quote: פעם אחת בערב יום הקדוש ערב
stories.summary_en: On Yom Kippur eve the hasidim begin Kol Nidre without their rebbe; he arrives late and explains that he heard a child left alone crying, so he stayed to play with it until it fell asleep.

tags.why: Set on Yom Kippur eve at Kol Nidre.
Kol Nidre prayer frames the story.
The point is the tzaddik's compassion, which he puts before arriving on time for prayer.

quotes: ויחמול הרבהקדוש על הילד וידבר עמו
tags.why: His compassion for a child is the virtue shown.

quotes: וידרשו וידרשי החסידים אחרי שרש דבר מה היה
tags.why: The hasidim learn afterwards why the rebbe was late.

quotes: כל החסידי׳ המסתופפים בצלו והם ממתינים
tags.why: The hasidim wait for their rebbe and ask him what happened.

quotes: הילד הלכה לבית התפלה והניחה הילד בוכה
tags.why: The child's mother is referred to as having gone to pray; she does not act on stage.

missing_concepts: care for children / compassion toward a child
putting kindness to a person before punctual communal prayer
a rebbe's custom that the congregation not wait for him
